title: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control
content: Access-control failures can permit unauthorized disclosure, modification, destruction, or execution beyond a user's intended permissions.

title: OWASP A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures
content: Missing or ineffective cryptographic protection can expose sensitive data at rest or in transit.

title: OWASP A03:2021 - Injection
content: Untrusted data interpreted as commands or queries can cause SQL, command, LDAP, and cross-site scripting injection.

title: OWASP A04:2021 - Insecure Design
content: Missing or ineffective security controls in system design cannot be fully corrected by implementation quality alone.

title: OWASP A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration
content: Unsafe defaults, unnecessary features, incomplete hardening, and verbose errors can expose systems to attack.

title: OWASP A06:2021 - Vulnerable and Outdated Components
content: Unknown, unsupported, or vulnerable component versions weaken the ability to assess and remediate application risk.

title: OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures
content: Weak identity, authentication, and session-management controls can allow account compromise.

title: OWASP A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures
content: Software updates, CI/CD pipelines, and serialized data require integrity verification and trusted provenance.

title: OWASP A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
content: Insufficient logging, monitoring, alerting, and incident integration can delay attack detection and response.

title: OWASP A10:2021 - Server-Side Request Forgery
content: Applications that fetch remote resources from unvalidated user input can be abused to reach unintended destinations.

title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
content: CSF 2.0 organizes cybersecurity outcomes through Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover functions.

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 - Incident Response
content: Incident response should be integrated across organizational risk management, with preparation and continuous improvement supporting detection, response, and recovery.

title: NIST SP 800-207 - Zero Trust Architecture
content: Zero trust grants no implicit trust based only on network location or ownership and evaluates access to resources explicitly.

title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 - Security and Privacy Controls
content: SP 800-53 provides a catalog of security and privacy controls for information systems and organizations.

title: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 - Risk Assessment
content: Risk assessment identifies threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, and impact to inform organizational risk decisions.

title: NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4 - Enterprise Patch Management
content: Enterprise patch management includes identifying, prioritizing, acquiring, installing, and verifying patches and related changes.

title: NIST SP 800-218 - Secure Software Development Framework
content: The SSDF groups secure development practices around preparing the organization, protecting software, producing well-secured software, and responding to vulnerabilities.

title: NIST SP 800-92 - Computer Security Log Management
content: Security log management covers generation, transmission, storage, analysis, and disposal of computer security log data.
